newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Sept 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Horse trainer Gai Waterhouse will run Juggler, All Our Mob and Sprint By as opponents for Filante in Saturday's A$300,000 George Main Stakes at Randwick, stating that she would not be handing a win to anybody. Page 22.

After Liverpool's 5-1 licking of Chelsea's unbeaten record on Saturday, Liverpool manager Roy Evans has stated Liverpool can do better, an ominous warning to all other English soccer premiership rivals. Page 23.

With Australia gaining a tie with Croatia on Saturday in the Davis Cup, Captain John Newcombe believes that Australia can win the cup next year. Mark Philippoussis won his game last night against Goran Oresic 6-1 6-4. Page 24.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Sea Eagles have beaten the Cronulla Sharks in a rugby league semi final match full of on-the-field violence. Manly dominated the match winning 24-0 and did not crumble as they did in last year's unexpected loss to Canterbury in the grand final. Page 26.

In the third round of the Loch Lomond world invitational yesterday, Australian golfer Robert Allenby held out for the day to finish in third place. Allenby hopes to make this tournament his fourth win for the year. Page 28.

World tennis number one, Monica Seles, showed once again why she is the come-back queen, beating world number two Arantxa Sanchez Vicario to regain the Japanese title she has won twice before. Page 30.
THE AGE

A nervous 24 hours is being waited out by Sydney's star defender, Andrew Dunkley, as the AFL scrutinises a videotape of the preliminary final game to see if Dunkley was in an off-the-ball incident with Essendon's James Hird. Page 3.

Sydney Swans captain Paul Kelly has been ordered by the AFL to fly to Melbourne to participate in the Brownlow Medal count, and has almost certainly set off a betting spree on the medal's outcome. Page 3.
The Adelaide Lightnings have won their third consecutive Women's National Basketball League grand final, overcoming the Sydney Flames on Saturday, 80-65, at the Sydney Entertainment Centre. Page 15.
HERALD SUN

With the AFL grand final less than a week away, North Melbourne will be hoping Corey McKernan stays well with his knee injury, while the Sydney Swans will be resting up key kicker Tony Lockett who has been suffering a groin injury for the past few weeks. age 96.

The National Basketball League yesterday warned all of its clubs that it would no longer tolerate clubs with substandard performances, poor venues and continued financial problems. The NBL has bought-out both the Geelong and Gold Coast teams for A$1 million. Page 88.

Australia has finished its four-nation Simba Cup program with class, beating the Kenya team 4-0 in Pretoria yesterday. The win took Australia to the top of the competition, but they were beaten in the end for the prize by South Africa, who drew their last game with Ghana 0-0. Page 90.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Race clubs in four States will begin their programs two hours early, with AFL grand final fever sure to take its normal viewers. This is a rare but sensible decision for the Australian Jockey Club. Page 40.

Reserve-grade coach for the Cronulla Sharks, Stuart Raper, continued his success with his team yesterday defeating Illawarra 24-8 in an elimination semi-final. The result means that for the sixth year in a row Raper will be involved in a rugby league grand final. Page 30.

Australia is regaining its former Davis Cup pride after yesterday's doubles win, with Mark Woodforde and Pat Rafter beating Croatia's Goran Ivanisevic and Sasa Hirzen, 6-3 6-2 6-4, in only 80 minutes. Page 38.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
